main_body: A tall strip of repeating wooden posts or boards with dark gaps, about 9px wide and 48px tall, drawn as a flat front view
top_band: none. At x=2 the top is a single light tan row (rows 0, 6, 12...) over a mid-brown face; at x=7 it is 2 light rows over 2 mid rows over dark. This is a 1-2px cap, not a surface.
evidence: The column scans show repeating 15-row units. Each unit has a 1-2 row light highlight, a 2-3 row mid-brown face, then dark brown or near-black fill. No horizontal surface is visible from above, and the beams have no top faces. A rim of 1-2px does not count as a top. It reads as a front-elevation fence or board pattern. It is not a frame with beams and a base showing top faces, so the kind also does not match.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile. The references have 38-40 colours and a median of 17-20 per tile. Shading is a light highlight, a mid tone and a dark fill, with no grain, speckle or per-plank variation. The dark areas are large uniform fills, even though the 5x5 flat-fill measure reads 0% because the units are narrow. The dark edges are tinted brown (0% neutral), so the outline is acceptable. The piece is still much shallower and flatter than the reference stall and well.
